single-choice-1.title: SQLite Type Names
single-choice-1.prompt: Which statement best describes declared column types in SQLite?
single-choice-1.hint: SQLite uses type affinity rather than the rigid type enforcement used by some database systems.

help.concept: SQLite accepts many declared type names and maps them to type affinities. This course uses INTEGER, REAL, and TEXT because their intent is clear.
help.hint_1: BOOLEAN can be declared, but SQLite stores boolean values as integers.
help.hint_2: Choose the statement that reflects SQLite's flexible typing model.

sketch0.title: CREATE TABLE turns a record design into typed columns
sketch0.bodyMarkdown:
A table definition names the records you want to store and the type of value each column accepts.

```sql
CREATE TABLE employees (
    id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    salary REAL
);
```

Here `INTEGER`, `TEXT`, and `REAL` describe the shape of each row. Start with the table and column design before adding stronger business constraints.

sketch1.title: sqlite_master shows the definition SQLite stored
sketch1.bodyMarkdown:
SQLite records table definitions in `sqlite_master`.

```sql
SELECT sql
FROM sqlite_master
WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'employees';
```

Inspecting the stored definition is useful when you want to confirm the actual schema rather than relying on memory.
